moments.cue: Sickle‑cell disease makes red cells stiff, blocking tiny vessels and causing pain.
In capillaries, sickled cells stick together, forming clogs that stop oxygen flow.
When a clog forms, patients feel excruciating pain, often in the chest or legs.
Doctors treat severe attacks with blood transfusions and hydroxyurea, which reduces sickling.
In 2023, gene‑editing therapy replaced faulty stem cells, offering a chance at a normal lifespan.
